summary.one_liner: Nmap is a network mapping and port scanning tool, installed from source with configure/make, with a bundled Zenmap graphical front-end.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Nmap as the Network Mapper, a command-line tool for scanning networks. Running "nmap scanme.nmap.org" is given as the basic example, and running nmap with no parameters prints a list of the most common options. The README points to a man page for in-depth option documentation. A graphical interface is available through the included Zenmap front-end. Binary installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux (RPM) are referenced on the Nmap.org website rather than in this repository. The README itself does not list specific scan types or features.
use_cases: scan a network to see which hosts are up
check which ports are open on a server
discover devices on a local network
run a graphical network scan with Zenmap
audit network exposure from the command line
notable: Mature, widely known network mapper with a built-in man page
Binary installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux (RPM) provided on Nmap.org
caveats: The license is custom and based on GPLv2 but not compatible with it; a commercial license is offered for redistributing Nmap in products
Detailed install and removal notes are on the external Nmap.org Install Guide rather than in the README
summary.license: Nmap Public Source License (custom, based on GPLv2 but not compatible with it)
keywords: see what is running on a server
